title: Knowing When ‘Good Enough’ Is Enough
scene: You have been polishing a presentation for longer than planned. You can still improve it, but you need to decide whether those small improvements are worth the extra time.
sceneJa: 資料を何度も修正していて、まだ改善できる点は残っている。ただ、『改善できる』ことと『さらに時間を使う価値がある』ことを分けて考え、やめどきを決める。

chunks.ja: 私はすでにプレゼン資料を修正していました
でも見つけ続けていました
自分に問いかけました
その変更に実際に気づくだろうか、と

chunks.en: would make the slides slightly better,
chunks.ja: スライドを少し良くするでしょう
でも、おそらく十分ではありません

chunks.en: to justify another hour of work.
chunks.ja: さらに1時間作業するだけの価値があるほどには
そこで、やめることにしました

chunks.en: when the presentation was clear and useful,
chunks.ja: プレゼン資料が分かりやすく、役に立つ状態になったところで

chunks.en: there was absolutely nothing left to improve.
chunks.ja: 改善できるところが完全になくなった

questions.question: Which boundary is most natural?
options: I asked myself / whether anyone other than me / would actually notice those changes
I asked / myself whether anyone / other than me would / actually notice those changes
I asked myself whether / anyone other / than me would actually notice
questions.explanation: ‘I asked myself’ is one thought unit, and the whether-clause gives the question the speaker asked internally.

questions.question: What does ‘not enough to justify another hour of work’ mean?
options: The speaker cannot work for another hour
The improvements exist, but they are not valuable enough to make another hour worthwhile
Another hour would make the presentation perfect
questions.explanation: ‘Enough to justify’ asks whether the benefit is large enough to make the extra cost—in this case, another hour—worthwhile.

questions.question: When does the speaker finally decide to stop?
options: When there is absolutely nothing left to improve
When someone else tells them to stop
When the presentation is clear and useful
questions.explanation: The speaker changes the stopping condition from perfection to usefulness: clear and useful is enough.

speak: Start slightly absorbed, as if you are still noticing tiny improvements. Pause at ‘Eventually, / I asked myself’ to mark the change in perspective. Read ‘not enough / to justify another hour of work’ thoughtfully, then make the final sentence sound calm and decisive rather than disappointed.
review: Previous normal lesson flow: reaction → consequence → comparison → priority. There, the key question changed from ‘What looks urgent?’ to ‘What happens if I do nothing?’ Today the question changes again: from ‘Can I make this better?’ to ‘Is the improvement worth the time?’ Better is often possible; worthwhile is a different test.
